clue.text: Put off by sight of French referee turning colour

parts.note: the French word for 'of' is de

indicators.note: turning tells us the short form of referee is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone is upset at the sight of a French referee going red in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses REF to give FER. 'by sight' just joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To put off a meeting is to postpone it until later, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Philosopher in fight at factory

definitions.meaning: John Stuart ... was a Victorian philosopher
old slang for a fistfight or boxing bout
a factory, as in a cotton or paper works

explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: 'in' and 'at' are just joining words.
explanation.definitionFit: Three separate senses of one word: the thinker J. S. Mill, a slang bout of fisticuffs, and a manufacturing works.

clue.text: Traveller with appearance to restore

parts.note: a rep, or commercial traveller, is a travelling salesperson
an air is a manner or appearance, as in an air of confidence

explanation.surface: A salesman whose good looks help him mend things.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore a damaged thing is to mend it, a plain synonym for the verb.

clue.text: Many are at liberty and without anxiety

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many

explanation.surface: Lots of people are free and have no worries.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without anxiety has no cares at all, a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Ill-behaved underworld attendant?

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the underworld itself
an orderly is a hospital attendant

explanation.surface: A question about a servant in the realm of the dead.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the whole clue also reads playfully as an attendant from Hades.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-behaved people are unruly and rowdy, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Radical journal with capacity to incite

parts.note: red is a label for a radical left-winger
a rag is a slang term for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A left-wing newspaper with the power to stir people up.
explanation.walkthrough: A red rag (to a bull) is something sure to provoke anger.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names something certain to provoke fury, so it has the power to inflame.

clue.text: It's laid down in mid-teens

indicators.note: in here is read as 'in disarray', telling us to rearrange the following letters

explanation.surface: A rule set down for teenagers of about fifteen.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of MIDTEENS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Silt or deposit is material settled or laid down in layers, so the cryptic description fits.

clue.text: Nothing in sport upset the soldiers

indicators.note: in places the round letter inside the turned word
upset in a down clue means the word sport is turned upside down, read bottom to top

explanation.surface: No sport has upset the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SPORT into TROPS; 'in' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers serving together are a body of armed men, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Cropped up in some Paris engagement

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something came up in a meeting in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that cropped up has appeared or emerged, a synonym in the past participle.

clue.text: Cut downhill

definitions.meaning: to cut a tree down is to bring it to the ground
a northern English word for a hill or moor, here read with 'down' as in tumbled, past tense of a verb for dropping

explanation.walkthrough: Fell means to cut down (a tree), and it is also the past tense of fall, went down, and a hill in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: chopping down a tree, and the past tense of tumbling down a slope.

clue.text: Quite honestly, it's over the committee's head

definitions.meaning: honestly and openly, with nothing hidden
read literally, something positioned higher than a committee

explanation.walkthrough: A double definition: the second reads the phrase literally as higher than the board of directors.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means openly and legitimately, with no deception, matching honestly.

clue.text: Bullet found in drawing office?

definitions.meaning: a bullet that leaves a visible trail of light
someone who copies drawings onto thin paper works in a drawing office

explanation.walkthrough: A double definition; the question mark marks the playful second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a luminous ammunition round, and a person who copies outlines through thin paper.

clue.text: Room can be found for wine

explanation.surface: Space must be made for the wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be found for' is just joining words. CHAMBERTIN is a red Burgundy.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated red Burgundy from Gevrey, so an example of the general class.

clue.text: Example of a grid map exercise

indicators.note: an exercise puts the letters through their paces, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A model case of a map-reading exercise on a grid.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of A GRID MAP are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A model or pattern serving as a standard case is a near synonym for example.

clue.text: Sweet wrapped in paper found in river

indicators.note: found in places the slang word for a paper inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
a rag is a slang term for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A sweet wrapped in newspaper is discovered in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrapped in' belongs to the sweet's picture and gives no letters; the container signal is 'found in'. The Dee is a river in Wales and England.
explanation.definitionFit: A sugar-coated sweet or almond, a type of confectionery.

clue.text: Eel, for example, can manoeuvre with grace

indicators.note: to manoeuvre is to move things about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An eel can move gracefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvre' rearranges EEL, EG and CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Grace of movement or manner is a close synonym for refinement.

clue.text: Fear of the first mistake

indicators.note: first takes only the opening letter of the word the

explanation.surface: A fear of making one's first error.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense fear or dread, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Gave up right to stop deer straying

parts.note: to end something is to stop it

indicators.note: straying means the letters of deer wander out of order

explanation.surface: The right to halt deer wandering is surrendered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'straying' rearranges DEER to ERED.
explanation.definitionFit: To render up is to hand over or surrender, as in rendering up a castle.

clue.text: Confidential comment smade when team entered

indicators.note: entered puts the team inside the word for when

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Private remarks passed when the team came in.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as published runs two words together: 'comment smade' should read 'comments made'.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarks muttered so only some can hear, as in stage whispers, are private comments.

clue.text: Replaced cobblers' hammers

indicators.note: replaced means the letters are put back in a different place

explanation.surface: Shoemakers' hammers have been swapped for new ones.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of COBBLERS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To clobber someone is to hit them hard, so the verb matches hammers.

clue.text: It may be made up in a general direction

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general

explanation.surface: A general heads in a particular direction.
explanation.walkthrough: Lost ground or delay is 'made up'; 'in a' is joining.
explanation.definitionFit: Lost time or distance, the margin to be recovered, is something one makes up.

clue.text: Attempting something difficult

definitions.meaning: hard to bear, as a tiresome day is

explanation.walkthrough: A double definition; 'something' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: having a go, and tiresome or hard to endure.

clue.text: Academic figure leading to link with Achilles?

indicators.note: leading puts the number ahead of the academic

parts.note: ten is a figure, a number
a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: A leading academic figure has a connection to the hero Achilles.
explanation.walkthrough: The Achilles tendon links the calf muscle to the heel.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of tissue connects muscle to bone, as in the Achilles one at the heel.

clue.text: Put up with danger erupting in a disorderly situation

parts.note: to bear something is to put up with it

indicators.note: erupting means the letters of danger burst out in a new order

explanation.surface: Tolerating danger as it breaks out in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erupting' rearranges DANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowdy, chaotic scene, from the old bear-baiting arenas, so a disorderly situation.

clue.text: Price novice pays for experience

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: The cost a beginner pays for gaining experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pays for' just joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To experience a sensation is to sense or undergo it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Just heard of nosh?

indicators.note: heard means we want a word that sounds like the synonym

explanation.surface: Fair word of some grub?
explanation.definitionFit: Food or fare, slang nosh, the food served at a meal.

clue.text: Crazy fellow getting one on account

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A man gets an extra entry on his bank account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' and 'on' are just joining words.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective it means wildly mad or frenzied.

clue.text: Point company pressed, but got beaten

parts.note: S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A firm was pressed hard and ended up thrashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' just joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be whipped or flogged is to be beaten, passive sense.
